solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Truth drug not in view

indicators.note: saying a thing is not in something tells you to take it out of that word

parts.note: a facet is one aspect or view of a matter
E is the usual slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone describes a truth serum that is kept out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Truth drug' reads as one phrase, but Truth is the definition alone: FACET loses its E to give FACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact is something known to be true, so the noun is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Reputation supported by award? One shows disbelief

indicators.note: in a down clue the upper part rests on what is beneath it, so the second word sits below the first

parts.note: to lose face is to lose reputation or standing
the palm is a traditional emblem of victory, as in the Palme d'Or

explanation.surface: A celebrity's good name is propped up by a prize, and someone looks on sceptically.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supported by' puts the award under the reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A facepalm, slapping a hand over the face, is the gesture people make on seeing something unbelievably foolish.

clue.text: Location of fifteenth inmate's instrument

parts.note: an inmate's location is a prison cell
the fifteenth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: We are asked where prisoner number fifteen keeps an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as the cell of the fifteenth letter: CELL then O.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is the large bowed string instrument played seated between the knees.

clue.text: Film across most of wrinkle in internal organ

indicators.note: taking most of a word means dropping its final letter

parts.note: to pan is to swing a camera across a scene while filming
a crease is a wrinkle in cloth or skin

explanation.surface: A camera sweeps over a wrinkle on some internal organ, as in a medical documentary.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas is the gland behind the stomach producing insulin and digestive enzymes, an organ inside the body.

clue.text: A new sport is ignored by a broadcaster

indicators.note: the little word is, being ignored, is struck out of the word next to it

parts.note: taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new
a racket sport
by places the article alongside

explanation.surface: A broadcaster decides to stop covering a newly popular sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is ignored' reads as a passive verb in the surface but tells you to drop the letters IS from TENNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna sends out radio or television signals, so it is literally a device that broadcasts.

clue.text: Political group, prats possibly, sheltered by body of people

indicators.note: something sheltered is held inside what protects it

parts.note: a community is a body of people living together

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters might come out in another arrangement

parts.note: fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A sneering remark that members of some party are idiots, protected by the public.
explanation.walkthrough: Prat is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The Communist Party is the name of political parties worldwide advocating communism, so it is a political group.

clue.text: Dirt beginning to collect, interrupting English lake's appearance

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which joins on here

parts.note: standard abbreviation
a mere is a lake, as in the Lake District's Windermere
gen is British slang for information, dirt as in gossip
first letter

explanation.surface: Muck starts to gather on an English lake and spoils its look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirt' looks like mud, but it is the gossip sense, as in 'have you got the dirt on him?'; gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergence is the act of coming into view, which is exactly what an appearance is.

clue.text: Fat? One's the ultimate in disgrace in matching clothes

indicators.note: in here means taking the place of, so one letter swaps in for another

parts.note: a suit is a matching jacket and trousers
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the ultimate is the last, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: Someone overweight, dressed in a matching outfit, is ultimately disgraced.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in SUIT is replaced by the final letter of disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Suet is the hard fat from around beef and mutton kidneys, used in British puddings and pastry.

clue.text: Duke's aria laying out bloodline and a new name

indicators.note: laying out things means setting them down in a fresh order
something new has been remade, so these letters take a different form

parts.note: fodder
fodder
fodder

explanation.surface: A nobleman's song sets out his family line and a new title.
explanation.walkthrough: Verdi's Rigoletto gives this famous aria to the Duke of Mantua.
explanation.definitionFit: La donna è mobile is the Duke of Mantua's celebrated tenor aria in Verdi's opera Rigoletto.

clue.text: No power in barmy story bearing new name at its top?

definitions.text: bearing new name at its top?

indicators.note: no power in a word means that strength-related piece is taken out of it

parts.note: barmy is British slang for crazy
arm means power or authority, as in the long arm of the law
a line is a story someone spins

explanation.surface: A crazy tale is given a fresh author's name at the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power' looks like electricity's P, but here it is strength in the sense of the long arm of the law.
explanation.definitionFit: A byline is the printed line at the head of a newspaper article giving the writer's name.

clue.text: Showed annoyance in kinky lacy gear in Canadian show

indicators.note: in places one group of letters inside the other
kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: fodder
to stamp the feet is to show annoyance

explanation.surface: Someone at a show in Canada was cross about racy lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram leaves one spare letter, which closes the answer after the inserted verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Calgary Stampede is an annual rodeo and exhibition in Alberta, Canada, billed as the greatest outdoor show on earth.

clue.text: New job advert

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a move up to a higher post
second meaning: publicity for a product

explanation.surface: It reads like a job listing in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Being moved up at work gives you a new job, while marketing publicity for a product is also called by this word.

clue.text: Strongly suggest, say, sport should be overhauled

indicators.note: hauled over means flipped end to end, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A recommendation that some game needs a thorough reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overhauled' looks like an anagram signal but is read as hauled over, a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone is to press them earnestly to do something, a firm recommendation.

clue.text: Gaps? Left a hint about new one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the following pieces

parts.note: standard abbreviation
taken as written
a cue is a prompt or hint
standard abbreviation
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone asks about gaps, having been dropped a hint about a fresh one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacunae, the Latin plural, are missing portions or blank spaces, as in a manuscript.

clue.text: Caught Welshman in melée heading off crossways?

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the remaining word
with its heading off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a scrum is a disorderly melee
C is caught in cricket scoring
Ifor is a Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A rugby report: a Welsh player is caught in a scrum as things turn sideways.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scorecards; Ifor is a traditional Welsh first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruciform means shaped like a cross, and the question mark admits crossways is a loose adjective for that.

clue.text: Rocket, article into most of constellation

indicators.note: into means put inside the other word
most of a word means losing its last letter

parts.note: Aries, the Ram, is a zodiac constellation
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A rocket launch pointed at a star pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariane is the series of European Space Agency launch vehicles, so it names a rocket.

clue.text: King deciding to face guillotine, restraining unsettled populace

indicators.note: the guillotine cuts off the head, so the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: chess abbreviation
settling a matter is deciding it

explanation.surface: A French king is about to be executed while the restless mob is held back.
explanation.walkthrough: Kettling is the British police tactic of penning protesters into a confined area.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettling is the police tactic of confining a crowd of protesters, holding back restless people within a cordon.

clue.text: Bird released in US sports event? Excellent

indicators.note: something released from inside escapes, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: the Super Bowl is American football's championship game
a nocturnal bird

explanation.surface: A bird is set free at a big American game.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb is an adjective of high praise meaning first-rate, a close synonym.

clue.text: Graduate books a long time seeing historic scientist

parts.note: Bachelor of Arts
B for book, doubled for the plural
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A graduate reserves a long stretch in the library reading about an old scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Babbage was the Victorian mathematician who designed early mechanical computers, an example of a pioneering scientist.

clue.text: Drunk's arrived? Hard cheese!

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
here means present, having arrived

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that the drunk has turned up, and gets a callous reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard cheese is British slang for tough luck, said without sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive retorts meaning tough luck, deal with it; the interjection matches the exclamation.

clue.text: Dessert's spherical shape in gel

indicators.note: in sets the first piece inside the following word

parts.note: to gel is to set firm
an orb is a sphere

explanation.surface: A pudding is a ball suspended in jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorbet is a frozen fruit-flavoured ice served as a pudding course after the main meal.

clue.text: Car fuel needing money invested, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front
the fuel word needs something put into it, taking it inside

parts.note: oil is fuel
M for money

explanation.surface: Running a car takes cash, someone concludes after thinking it over.
explanation.definitionFit: A limo is the short form of limousine, a large luxurious chauffeured motor vehicle.

clue.text: Source of attraction in part of London probed by publication

indicators.note: a thing probed has something pushed inside it

parts.note: Barnet is a borough of north London
a mag is a magazine

explanation.surface: A magazine investigates what draws people to a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of attraction' sounds like a tourist sight; it is magnetic attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar magnet is a straight bar of magnetised metal, which literally exerts magnetic attraction.

clue.text: Island shared between Argentina and Uruguay

indicators.note: shared between two names means part comes from each, the end of one and the start of the other

parts.note: the closing letters
the opening letters

explanation.surface: An island claimed jointly by two South American neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: It is not a strict hidden word, since the 'and' interrupts: the tail of one country joins the head of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a tiny island republic in the central Pacific Ocean, one of the smallest nations on earth.

clue.text: Secconds, dessert? Not this food

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for seconds (the source's spelling has a doubled C)
pud is British slang for pudding, dessert

explanation.surface: Someone offered second helpings of pudding declines that dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not this' is a joke: the answer built from S and PUD is a potato, not a dessert at all. A spud is a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is informal for a potato, a staple vegetable eaten as food.

clue.text: Star represented in American tour pix

indicators.note: something represented is shown again in another form, so the letters are redrawn

parts.note: fodder

explanation.surface: A celebrity appears in holiday snaps from a trip around the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity, but it is the astronomical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Proxima Centauri is a red dwarf, the nearest star to the Sun, about 4.2 light years away.

clue.text: Mother to look round rear of cistern for wet blanket

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

indicators.note: the rear is the back end, so just the final letter is wanted

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: A mother inspects a water tank, finding something to spoil the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is a person or thing that spoils fun, and a dampener likewise deadens enthusiasm.

clue.text: Part of body, note, located within ear

indicators.note: located within means set inside the next word

parts.note: lug is informal British for an ear
N for note

explanation.surface: An anatomy lesson: a musical note sits inside the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The lung is one of the paired breathing organs in the chest, an internal component of the body.
